correctness.rationale: The finite-flag orbit-barycenter lemma gives a PL homeomorphism between |X_r|^{<g>} and the flag complex on complete admissible vertex orbits: fixed barycentric coefficients are constant on each orbit. A nonidentity rotation of order L>=4 has within-orbit diameter floor(L/2)*(3r/L)>r; L=2 has antipodal diameter 3r/2>r; L=3 yields exactly r mutually incompatible admissible triples T_i. For r=2h even, the s_0 reflection admissible orbits split into vertex-axis A_0..A_h and antipodal-axis B_0..B_h, each forming a clique, with exactly cross-pairs (A_0,B_h) and (A_h,B_0). Two contractible simplices connected by two separate edges deformation-retract onto S^1. Edge-axis s_1 yields two disjoint simplices (S^0). For r=2h+1 odd, one conjugacy class has two cliques joined by exactly one cross-edge, hence contractible. Cases r=2,3 included. Adamaszek Corollary 6.7 supplies wedge^(r-1)S^2; finite-group simplicial Lefschetz gives tr(g|H~_2)=χ(|X_r|^g)-1, agreeing with the previously published signed augmentation character. Independently enumerated all rotations and reflections and full clique-complex GF(2) homology for 2<=r<=16 (390 rotations and 405 reflections), with matching ranks; this finite enumeration corroborates but is not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS strictly for the uniform all-r geometric REFLECTION fixed-space classification (odd-r contractible; even-r vertex-axis S^1, edge-axis S^0), the genuinely new central statement. The identity wedge is Adamaszek 2011, all rotational fixed spaces are covered by the earlier all-scale rotational persistence theorem, and the ENTIRE displayed rational character is identically published in the November 1 signed augmentation-lattice theorem. Neither this character nor the rotation cases receive novelty credit. The character determines fixed Euler characteristics only and cannot force a particular reflection-fixed homotopy type; the new exact orbit-compatibility-graph classification provides that missing geometry. The 2014 nerve-dihedral homology theorem concerns another complex; its Theorem 8.5 is not an equivariant identification preserving the full original dihedral action. Bounded Resultary searches found the assigned record itself, earlier related structures, and no earlier all-r reflection fixed-space theorem. Historical priority remains best-of-knowledge.

value.rationale: The first one-third critical Rips family Cl(C_(3r)^r) is a canonical natural filtration boundary with ambient wedge of 2-spheres. A complete all-parameter reflection-fixed homotopy classification reveals an S^1 loop for even vertex-axis involutions, disconnected fixed space for even edge-axis involutions and contractible fixed space for odd cycles. Those homotopy/connectivity distinctions are invisible to both ambient nonequivariant homotopy and the previously known full dihedral character (only Euler characteristics). The exact orbit-compatibility graph analysis is a substantive geometric invariant and a useful model for equivariant topology, not a finite table extension or routine character calculation. The latter known character is not counted as independent value or novelty.

limitations: Primary novelty is the uniform reflection-fixed space classification; the rotation fixed-space subclaims and the entire rational character had been published earlier and are not claimed as original in this assessment. The source package is scientifically correct but its earlier relationship-to-prior prose undercredits these two sources.
Finite computations through r=16 confirm selected GF2 homology but do not prove the infinite parameter family; the all-r result rests on exact orbit-distance and clique-boundary arguments.

An unindexed source might contain the exact reflection orbit classification; all originality conclusions are best-of-knowledge only. No scientific claim about subgroup fixed intersections or integral equivariant splitting beyond the cited known lattice.
